correctness.rationale: For every odd m>=5, h_P(-v_j)=cos(pi/m). Thus each vertex translate excludes the strict interior of the concentric polygon with vertex-normal support h=1-t cos(pi/m). In the nearest-vertex sector, the intersection of (1+t)P with X>=h is a five-vertex polygon: A=(1+t,0), E_±=(1+t)(cos²theta,±cos theta sin theta), H_±=(h,±h tan theta). A and E_± belong to v_0+tP by explicit convex combinations; H_± lie on its opposite edge because 1<=2t cos theta for t>=1. Convexity establishes coverage outside the hole, including its boundary. At t=sec theta the center becomes covered; addition of (t-sec theta)P proves all larger dilations convexify. For 0<=t<1 an outer polygon edge has a central uncovered segment, so no earlier convexification. The inradius-area calculation gives m(1-t cos theta)^2 tan theta, and normalization and theta-series give the exact relative law and both fourth-order asymptotics. No finite geometry experiment is used as proof.
